paragraphs.text: Customize Latin and CJK UI fonts, code fonts, and font sizes in DeepSeek Harness, with live previews
and automatic saving.
# dsh-custom-fonts
Change the **Latin** and **CJK** UI fonts, the **code font**, and the **text size** of the DeepSeek
Harness (DSH) Web UI from a settings page. Changes show up live and are saved automatically.
> A maintained fork of lsh2002/dsh-custom-fonts that adds settings persistence and an English UI. Se
ined fork of lsh2002/dsh-custom-fonts that adds settings persistence and an English UI. See Credits.
## Features

- **Separate fonts** for Latin text, CJK text (Chinese, Japanese, Korean), and code.
- **Font size o

ffset** from -4 to +8 px, applied evenly to all text.
- **Tight-spacing fix for session titles** (op
tional, for Safari and the macOS desktop app): WebKit squeezes characters in truncated titles; with

this on, titles fade out at the edge instead of ending in "…".
- **Live preview** with Latin, Japane

se, Chinese, Korean, and code samples.
- **Installed-font suggestions** in any browser on the comput
er DSH runs on (including the macOS desktop app), each shown in its own typeface. Fonts that fit the
field come first (Japanese/Chinese/Korean fonts for CJK, monospaced fonts for code), with JP/SC/TC/

KR/Mono tags. Japanese font names such as 游ゴシック work too.
- **Saved automatically** in your DSH prof
ile and restored after a reload or restart.
## Install
Replace `web` with your DSH profile name (the desktop app uses `desktop`).
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then **restart DSH** once. The plugin needs to be loaded before it can save settings.
> Coming from upstream 1.0 or 1.1? Those versions never saved anything. Run the command above to rep
lace them, restart DSH, and enter your fonts again.
## Usage

1. Open **Settings → Fonts**.
2. Type a font name, pick a suggestion, or enter a comma-separated lis

t such as `Inter, Segoe UI`. An empty field keeps the default font.
3. Installed fonts are listed au
tomatically on the computer DSH runs on. From another device, click **Detect installed fonts** (Chro

me and Edge) to use that device's fonts.
4. Move the **Font size offset** slider. `0px` means no cha

nge.
5. Use **Restore defaults** to undo everything.
## Troubleshooting
| Symptom | What to do |

| The **Fonts** page is missing | Restart DSH after installing, then refresh the page. |
| Changes a
pply but are lost on reload | Check the status line at the bottom of the page. DSH saves settings on

ly from a local (loopback) connection, and only after restarting once with the plugin installed. |
|
"Could not save font settings" | Edit any setting to try again. If it keeps failing, check the entr

y in `cordis.patch.yml` for a wrong value type. |
| Font name has no effect | Check the spelling, or

pick it from the suggestions to see which names are installed. |
| Suggestions show only a few comm
on fonts | The installed-font list needs DSH restarted once after updating the plugin. From another
device, use Chrome or Edge and click **Detect installed fonts**. |
For the status messages and the stored format, see How it works.
## Uninstall
[代码示例省略，未执行]
You can also remove it from **Settings → Plugins**. After a refresh the original fonts return. The s
aved entry may remain in `cordis.patch.yml`, and you can delete it.
